the accumulation of heavy metals in plants and the antioxidant response to heavy metals.
the bioaccumulation of heavy metals in the leaves of two species of plants, C. arenosa and P. lanceolataliving in metalliferous soils of the former mining area of Rudniki, Poland.

the antioxidative defense system of C. arenosas and P. lanceolatas leaves is not a simple and direct response to the metal contamination, but it is a complex response to the metal stress.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the plants from metalliferous sites have the potential to be used in phytostablization of metal-contaminated soils and that they have developed a complex antioxidant defense system against the toxic effects of heavy metals.
the studied species are tolerant towards heavy metals, and that they could be used in the phytoremediation of heavy metal-contaminated sites.
the antioxidative system is involved in heavy metal stress response in the plants and that the studied species are suitable for phytostabilizing heavy metals.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the concentrations of metals in soil and their availability in the soil solution are not always correlated with the metal concentrations in plants, which is a very important aspect for the use of plants for the remediation of heavy metal-contaminated soil.

the plants C. arenosa and P. lanceolato are able to grow on metalliferous soil and to accumulate heavy metals, which is an important factor for the development of phytostabilisation techniques in metalliferous sites.
the concentrations of the examined metals in soil, their potential bioavailability, and their bioaccumulation in plant tissues are not always correlated.
